title: Shelter Buddies
intro: Text 1 is a webpage inviting teenagers to volunteer with shelter animals.

visual.text: SHELTER BUDDIES · A PROGRAMME FOR TEENS AGED 14 TO 17
He has been waiting a long time for someone to learn his name.
Give two Sunday mornings a month to a shelter dog or cat that nobody has chosen yet.
A thin brown dog presses its nose through the bars of a kennel. A name card on the gate reads ‘Kopi — here since last year’. A teenager’s hand reaches towards it.

Shelters are full of animals that are fed and safe but rarely touched. Volunteers are few, and the shy ones at the back get the least attention. As a Shelter Buddy, you are matched with one animal for six months. You walk it, brush it, sit beside it, and write a short note after each visit. Those notes help the shelter find it a home.

visual.title: Before you sign up
items: This is not a petting zoo. You will clean kennels and wash bowls.
Some animals will take weeks to trust you.
You need a parent’s consent and closed shoes.
You may not adopt your buddy — but your notes may help someone else to.

visual.text: “For three visits Kopi would not come near me. On the fourth, he fell asleep on my foot. I did not move for an hour.” — Sarah, 16
Apply to be a Shelter Buddy

text2.intro: Text 2 is taken from a letter that a family wrote to an animal shelter after adopting a dog.
paragraphs: We nearly walked past Kopi. He was curled up at the back of his kennel and did not even lift his head when we called. Then one of your staff showed us the notebook hanging on his gate. Page after page, a volunteer called Sarah had written about him: that he was scared of brooms, that he loved having his ears rubbed, that he slept better with an old towel. Reading those notes made us feel we already knew him, and we took him home that same afternoon.
Three months on, he still hides whenever the broom comes out, but he waits by the door every evening for us. Please pass on our thanks to Sarah. — The Lim family

questions.text: Look at Text 1. Which sentence best states the main message of the webpage?

options.label: A
options.text: Teenagers can adopt the animal they look after once six months are up.

options.label: B
options.text: Shelter animals need patient, regular company, and teenagers can give it.

options.label: C
options.text: Shelters need donations of money more than they need volunteers.

scheme.answer: Shelter animals need patient, regular company, and teenagers can give it.

questions.text: Look at the picture in Text 1. How does it support the headline ‘He has been waiting a long time for someone to learn his name.’?

scheme.answer: The name card says Kopi has been there since last year, and he pushes his nose through the bars towards a hand, showing he has waited a long time and longs for someone to notice him.
accept: The card shows he has been in the shelter since last year, so he has been waiting a long time, and he reaches out to the teenager’s hand because he wants someone of his own.
His name card and his nose pressed through the bars show a dog that has waited long and is eager for a person to know him.

seeds.text: The card on the gate says Kopi has been there since last year, and he is pushing his nose out to the hand, so it shows he has been waiting long and wants someone to care about him.
We can see from the sign that the dog has stayed in the shelter for over a year, and he is trying to reach the person, so he is lonely and hoping for a friend.
It shows that the dog is dangerous and should be kept behind bars.
The picture shows a dog in a shelter.
A thin brown dog presses its nose through the bars of a kennel.
